sentences.text: It is submitted by the counsel for the appellants that since the appellants were not in possession of money to pay the Court fees, therefore they could not file the appeal within stipulated period.
It is submitted that there is a delay of 66 days in filing the appeal and the appellants may not be made to suffer on account of their poverty.
3. Per contra, the application is vehemently opposed by the counsel for the respondent.

4. Considering the fact that the delay is only of 66 days and the appellants have lost their son and they were also required to make arrangement for finances, therefore the delay of 66 days in filing the appeal is hereby condoned.

5. This Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act has been filed against the award dated 07/05/2019 passed by Second Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Burhanpur, in M.A.C.C. No.84/2018, for enhancement.

entities.text:
Second Additional Member Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Burhanpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 6. Since the factum of accident is not in dispute, therefore it is suffice to mention here that the deceased - Rajesh met with a vehicular accident on 04/07/2018 and lost his life.
The age of the deceased was 23 years.

7. It is submitted by the counsel for the appellants that the Claims Tribunal has assessed the monthly notional income of the deceased as Rs.6,000/- but as per the Minimum Wages Act, the monthly income of an unskilled labour was Rs.7,325/- on the date of accident.
Therefore, the notional income taken by the Claims Tribunal is on lower side and accordingly, it is submitted that the award may be enhanced by further amount of Rs.1,00,000/-.
8. Per contra, the appeal is vehemently opposed by the counsel for the respondent.

9. Heard the learned counsel for the parties.
10.

The counsel for the appellants is right in making a submission that for assessing the notional income of the deceased, the Tribunal can consider the notification issued by the State Government under the Minimum Wages Act.
11. The accident took place on 04/07/2018 and as per the notification, the monthly income of an unskilled labour was Rs.7,325/-.
After adding 40% by way of future prospect, the monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.10,255/-.

Since the deceased was a bachelor and therefore, his personal expenses would be half and thus his monthly loss of income comes to Rs.5,127.50/-, and accordingly, his yearly loss of income comes to Rs.61,530/-.

Since the deceased was aged 23 years,
therefore the multiplier of 18 would apply and the total loss of income would come to Rs.11,07,540/-, whereas the Claims Tribunal has awarded Rs.9,07,200/- towards loss of income.
12. Since the appellants have valued the appeal at Rs.1,00,000/-, therefore the compensation amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal is enhanced by further amount of Rs.1,00,000/-.
